title: Pipeline design doc — gf2-sim
description:
## Goal

Land a single design document for the `gf2-sim` pipeline that
locks the architecture contract before Phase A (CPU foundation)
and Phase B (GPU stages) start in parallel. This is the only
Phase 0 task; both subsequent phases gate against it.

## Context

Parent epic: `f9717e7e` — *Research-grade CPU+GPU FEC simulation
pipeline (gf2-sim)*. The 15-row locked-architecture table in the
epic description is the input contract; this doc expands it into
implementable detail.

The design doc must answer enough that two independent worker
streams (CPU foundation, GPU stages) can build to a single
contract without integration drift in Phase C.

## Deliverables

Single markdown document at
`dev/active/<short-id>-pipeline-design.md`, attached to this
issue via `jit doc add`. Sections:

1. **Stage / Connector trait shapes.**
   - `trait Stage<I, O>` signature; `process_batch(&self, &I) -> O`
     vs streaming.
   - `Connector` type carrying SoA-layout metadata + batch size +
     numeric precision.
   - Error type hierarchy (recoverable vs fatal; OOM is
     recoverable, kernel error is fatal).
   - How stages declare their preferred layout and how the
     executor inserts layout converters.

2. **SoA ↔ AoS conversions at user-visible I/O.**
   - Where exactly the transpose happens (entry / exit of the
     pipeline; never inside a stage).
   - Cost model: one transpose per batch boundary on the user side;
     zero inside the pipeline.
   - Memory ownership: pipeline owns SoA buffers; user owns AoS.

3. **ChaCha20 per-worker seek scheme.**
   - Stream partitioning: per-(SNR, worker) sub-stream via
     `ChaCha20Rng::set_word_pos(base + worker_idx * chunk_words)`.
   - Choice of `chunk_words` (≥ 2^32 to give each worker its own
     2^96-state subspace under fixed seed; or fixed-per-config
     constant).
   - Same scheme on GPU: kernel computes its starting offset from
     `(snr_idx, worker_idx, frame_offset_in_chunk)`.

4. **Heartbeat-checkpoint schema in the streaming pipeline.**
   - Backwards compatibility with existing
     `checkpoints/snr_NNNN.json` shape from issue `fd73e8a8` if
     possible; otherwise new schema with migration rule.
   - How checkpoint write interacts with GPU pipeline draining
     (flush in-flight batches before serialising the SNR-point
     state).
   - Per-SNR-boundary + within-SNR heartbeat granularity, both
     supported.

5. **Crate-boundary diagram.**
   - `gf2-core` (primitives) ← `gf2-coding` (codes) ← `gf2-sim`
     (pipeline + executor).
   - `gf2-sim` optional dep on `gf2-kernels-hip` behind feature
     `hip`.
   - Public surface of each crate (what `gf2-sim` exports vs hides).
   - Test crate boundaries: `cargo test --workspace` works on
     non-ROCm hosts (HIP feature off by default).

6. **Multi-arch HIP dispatch.**
   - Compile-time gfx target list (gfx1030 today; gfx1100, gfx1200,
     gfx9{0,4}a planned).
   - Runtime detection: `hipDeviceGetAttribute` for compute
     capability; selects the best-fit kernel variant.
   - "Unsupported arch" behaviour: fall back to CPU stage with
     `tracing::warn` (consistent with OOM policy).

7. **Multi-GPU extension seams.**
   - Single-GPU is the v1 implementation. Document the exact
     seams that admit multi-GPU later:
     - Stream pool generalises to per-device pools.
     - Worker → device assignment becomes user-configurable.
     - Aggregation step is already device-agnostic.
   - No multi-GPU code lands in v1; design verifies no decision
     forecloses it.

8. **Failure-mode policy.**
   - OOM: catch from `hipMalloc`; fall back to CPU stage for the
     current batch; `tracing::warn!` event with batch ID, SNR
     index, device ID; continue.
   - Kernel error / driver error: log full diagnostic dump (HIP
     error code + last-known kernel launch args + device state);
     hard fail the run; non-zero exit code.
   - Per-run CLI flag to override OOM auto-fallback to hard-fail
     (for reproducibility-critical experiments).

9. **Layered builder-vs-graph API surfaces.**
   - Typestate builder for presets (DVB-T2, 5G NR, 802.11n):
     compile-time type safety; method chaining.
   - Graph API for novel chains: `Chain::new().add_stage().connect()`;
     runtime type-check on `connect`.
   - The builder is generated from / consistent with the graph API
     (presets are just pre-wired graphs with typestate wrappers).
   - Example: DVB-T2 BICM chain expressed in both APIs.

10. **Numerical precision strategy.**
    - f32 LLR by default (matches existing); f64 via cargo feature
      `llr-f64` (matches existing).
    - Mixed-precision deferred to a future task; document the
      seam.

11. **Determinism contract summary** (re-stated for code-review
    convenience).

12. **Migration plan from `simulation.rs`** — what subset of the
    existing simulation runner moves into `gf2-sim` vs stays in
    `gf2-coding`; how `e4849f07` and the campaign binary pick up
    the new pipeline in Phase D.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Design doc lands at
  `dev/active/<short-id>-pipeline-design.md`, attached via
  `jit doc add` to this issue.
- [hard] All 12 sections above present with implementable detail
  (no "TBD" or "TODO" leaves; if a decision is intentionally
  deferred, the doc names the follow-up task and what triggers
  revisiting).
- [hard] All 15 interview decisions from the parent epic's
  locked-architecture table are explicitly cited with one-line
  rationale.
- [hard] At least two API-style examples shown side-by-side:
  same DVB-T2 BICM chain expressed via (a) typestate builder
  preset and (b) raw graph API.
- [hard] Crate-boundary diagram included (Mermaid `graph TD` or
  ASCII).
- [hard] User reviews and approves before Phase A and Phase B
  kick off.
- [hard] `doc-review` gate passes.

## Non-goals

- No code in this task. The doc is the entire deliverable.
- No prototype kernels.
- No multi-GPU implementation (seams only).
- No 5G NR or 802.11n preset detail (those are Phase E concerns).
